trigger.message: Skill 'aws-waf-log-analysis' was NOT triggered (no skills were loaded)

expected_output.reasoning: The investigation's root cause finding precisely matches the expected root cause: it identifies the security group sg-0123456789abcdef0 (origin NLB SG) being narrowed at 16:04:43 UTC and reverted at 16:28:37 UTC as the cause of CloudFront timeouts/connection failures, correctly noting the absence of a 5xx error rise and ruling out WAF (CloudFront 4xx stayed flat at 0%, no WAF blocks mentioned as cause). Key identifying details (SG ID, timestamps, mechanism, and lack of WAF involvement) all align with the expected root cause.
expected_output.evidence: "At 2026-10-11 16:04:43 UTC, rule sgr-076ace4b66a382b12 (TCP port 80) was narrowed from 0.0.0.0/0 to 192.0.2.10/32... At 16:28:37 UTC the same rule was reverted to 0.0.0.0/0... CloudFront error rates stayed near zero throughout (a single 0.46% TotalErrorRate blip at 16:05, 4xx flat at 0%)."

assertion_results.text: The Root Cause names the security group change on the origin load balancer at about 16:04 UTC (sg-0123456789abcdef0 ingress narrowed) as the cause of the timeouts
assertion_results.evidence: 'Root Cause: Operator restricted ui NLB security group to a single IP, blocking CloudFront' ... 'At 2026-10-11 16:04:43 UTC, rule sgr-076ace4b66a382b12 (TCP port 80) was narrowed from 0.0.0.0/0 to 192.0.2.10/32, blocking all other sources — including CloudFront's edge IPs'
assertion_results.reasoning: The output explicitly names sg-0123456789abcdef0, the time ~16:04 UTC, and the ingress narrowing as the root cause of the timeouts.

assertion_results.text: A finding or Supporting Observation ties the onset and the recovery to the security group change and its revert (about 16:04 and about 16:28 UTC), not only the onset
assertion_results.evidence: 'At 16:28:37 UTC the same rule was reverted to 0.0.0.0/0, restoring access... the 16:28:37 revert restored origin reachability and traffic recovered by ~16:29–16:30.' Also symptom section notes 'recovery begins 16:31... fully recovered ~16:33'
assertion_results.reasoning: The finding explicitly ties both the onset (16:04:43) and the revert/recovery (16:28:37, recovery ~16:29-16:33) to the security group change and its reversal, not just the onset.

assertion_results.text: Supporting Observations cite front-door or load-balancer metric evidence for the outage (for example the CloudFront request drop, load balancer flow counts or target health) and the CloudTrail event for the security group change
assertion_results.evidence: Symptom section cites CloudFront request volume metrics ('collapsed from a steady ~2,400 req/min baseline to as low as 63 req/min... onset at 16:05 UTC... trough ~63 req/min at 16:18, recovery begins 16:31') and the Root Cause finding cites 'CloudTrail shows two ModifySecurityGroupRules events on sg-0123456789abcdef0... rule sgr-076ace4b66a382b12'
assertion_results.reasoning: Both CloudFront metric evidence and CloudTrail event evidence are cited to support the finding.

assertion_results.text: No finding attributes the timeouts to an AWS WAF rule or action; if WAF is examined, it is ruled out with evidence (Blocked, Challenge and CAPTCHA counts flat or zero, or all traffic allowed)
assertion_results.evidence: 'CloudFront error rates stayed near zero throughout (a single 0.46% TotalErrorRate blip at 16:05, 4xx flat at 0%). This signature... is consistent with connection failures/timeouts... NOT CloudFront-returned 5xx origin errors or 4xx/WAF blocks.' No finding attributes the issue to WAF; the root cause is clearly the security group change.
assertion_results.reasoning: The output explicitly rules out WAF/4xx blocks as the cause using flat 4xx and near-zero error rate evidence, and attributes the cause entirely to the security group change instead.
